pattern_rules.rule: `*` matches zero or more characters but never `/`.
pattern_rules.quote: `*`: Matches zero or more characters, but does not match the `/` character. For example, `Octo*` matches `Octocat`.

pattern_rules.rule: `**` matches zero or more of any character, including `/`.
pattern_rules.quote: `**`: Matches zero or more of any character.

pattern_rules.rule: `?` matches zero or one of the preceding character (regex-like quantifier, not a single-char wildcard).
pattern_rules.quote: `?`: Matches zero or one of the preceding character.

pattern_rules.rule: `+` matches one or more of the preceding character.
pattern_rules.quote: `+`: Matches one or more of the preceding character.

pattern_rules.rule: `[]` is a character class of alphanumerics; ranges are limited to a-z, A-Z, 0-9.
pattern_rules.quote: `[]` Matches one alphanumeric character listed in the brackets or included in ranges. Ranges can only include `a-z`, `A-Z`, and `0-9`. For example, the range`[0-9a-z]` matches any digit or lowercase letter. For example, `[CB]at` matches `Cat` or `Bat` and `[1-2]00` matches `100` and `200`.

pattern_rules.rule: `!` negates only when it is the first character of a pattern; elsewhere it is literal.
pattern_rules.quote: `!`: At the start of a pattern makes it negate previous positive patterns. It has no special meaning if not the first character.

pattern_rules.rule: YAML quoting: patterns starting with `*`, `[` or `!` must be quoted; in a flow sequence any pattern containing `[` or `]` must be quoted, otherwise the workflow fails to parse.
pattern_rules.quote: The characters `*`, `[`, and `!` are special characters in YAML. If you start a pattern with `*`, `[`, or `!`, you must enclose the pattern in quotes. Also, if you use a flow sequence with a pattern containing `[` and/or `]`, the pattern must be enclosed in quotes.

pattern_rules.rule: Unquoted `**/README.md` or unquoted `release/v[0-9].[0-9]` inside `[ ]` is a parse error that prevents the workflow from running (docs example block).
pattern_rules.quote:
# Valid
paths:
  - '**/README.md'

# Invalid - creates a parse error that
# prevents your workflow from running.
paths:
  - **/README.md

# Valid
branches: [ main, 'release/v[0-9].[0-9]' ]

# Invalid - creates a parse error
branches: [ main, release/v[0-9].[0-9] ]

pattern_rules.rule: Ordering of negation (branches): a negative match after a positive match excludes; a positive match after a negative match re-includes.
pattern_rules.quote:
The order that you define patterns matters.

* A matching negative pattern (prefixed with `!`) after a positive match will exclude the Git ref.
* A matching positive pattern after a negative match will include the Git ref again.

pattern_rules.rule: Ordering of negation (paths): same sequential semantics as branches.
pattern_rules.quote:
The order that you define `paths` patterns matters:

* A matching negative pattern (prefixed with `!`) after a positive match will exclude the path.
* A matching positive pattern after a negative match will include the path again.

pattern_rules.rule: Ordering of negation (workflow_run branches): same sequential semantics.
pattern_rules.quote:
The order that you define patterns matters.

* A matching negative pattern (prefixed with `!`) after a positive match will exclude the branch.
* A matching positive pattern after a negative match will include the branch again.

pattern_rules.rule: Path cheat sheet restates sequential evaluation and re-inclusion.
pattern_rules.quote: Patterns are checked sequentially. A pattern that negates a previous pattern will re-include file paths.

pattern_rules.rule: A `branches` list that uses `!` must contain at least one positive pattern; exclusion-only lists belong in `branches-ignore`.
pattern_rules.quote: If you define a branch with the `!` character, you must also define at least one branch without the `!` character. If you only want to exclude branches, use `branches-ignore` instead.

pattern_rules.rule: Same at-least-one-positive rule for `tags` with `!`.
pattern_rules.quote: Similarly, if you define a tag with the `!` character, you must also define at least one tag without the `!` character. If you only want to exclude tags, use `tags-ignore` instead.

pattern_rules.rule: Same at-least-one-positive rule for `paths` with `!`.
pattern_rules.quote: If you define a path with the `!` character, you must also define at least one path without the `!` character. If you only want to exclude paths, use `paths-ignore` instead.

pattern_rules.rule: `branches` and `branches-ignore` are mutually exclusive on the same event (pull_request / pull_request_target).
pattern_rules.quote: Use the `branches` filter when you want to include branch name patterns or when you want to both include and exclude branch names patterns. Use the `branches-ignore` filter when you only want to exclude branch name patterns. You cannot use both the `branches` and `branches-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow.

pattern_rules.rule: `branches`/`branches-ignore` and `tags`/`tags-ignore` are each mutually exclusive pairs on `push`.
pattern_rules.quote:
Use the `branches` filter when you want to include branch name patterns or when you want to both include and exclude branch names patterns. Use the `branches-ignore` filter when you only want to exclude branch name patterns. You cannot use both the `branches` and `branches-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow.

Use the `tags` filter when you want to include tag name patterns or when you want to both include and exclude tag names patterns. Use the `tags-ignore` filter when you only want to exclude tag name patterns. You cannot use both the `tags` and `tags-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow.

pattern_rules.rule: `paths` and `paths-ignore` are mutually exclusive on the same event.
pattern_rules.quote: Use the `paths` filter when you want to include file path patterns or when you want to both include and exclude file path patterns. Use the `paths-ignore` filter when you only want to exclude file path patterns. You cannot use both the `paths` and `paths-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow. If you want to both include and exclude path patterns for a single event, use the `paths` filter prefixed with the `!` character to indicate which paths should be excluded.

pattern_rules.rule: `branches` and `branches-ignore` are mutually exclusive on `workflow_run`; use `!` inside `branches` to combine.
pattern_rules.quote: You cannot use both the `branches` and `branches-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow. If you want to both include and exclude branch patterns for a single event, use the `branches` filter along with the `!` character to indicate which branches should be excluded.

pattern_rules.rule: On `push`: defining only a branch filter means tag pushes never run (and vice versa); defining neither runs for both; branch filter AND path filter must both pass.
pattern_rules.quote: If you define only `tags`/`tags-ignore` or only `branches`/`branches-ignore`, the workflow won't run for events affecting the undefined Git ref. If you define neither `tags`/`tags-ignore` or `branches`/`branches-ignore`, the workflow will run for events affecting either branches or tags. If you define both `branches`/`branches-ignore` and `paths`/`paths-ignore`, the workflow will only run when both filters are satisfied.

pattern_rules.rule: On pull_request / pull_request_target: branch filter AND path filter must both be satisfied.
pattern_rules.quote: If you define both `branches`/`branches-ignore` and `paths`/`paths-ignore`, the workflow will only run when both filters are satisfied.

pattern_rules.rule: Branch/tag patterns are evaluated against the Git ref's name (refs/heads/..., refs/tags/...), i.e. the short name after the prefix.
pattern_rules.quote:
The patterns defined in `branches` and `tags` are evaluated against the Git ref's name. For example, the following workflow would run whenever there is a `push` event to:

* A branch named `main` (`refs/heads/main`)
* A branch named `mona/octocat` (`refs/heads/mona/octocat`)
* A branch whose name starts with `releases/`, like `releases/10` (`refs/heads/releases/10`)
* A tag named `v2` (`refs/tags/v2`)
* A tag whose name starts with `v1.`, like `v1.9.1` (`refs/tags/v1.9.1`)

pattern_rules.rule: For pull_request/pull_request_target the branch filter matches the pull request's TARGET (base) branch, not the head branch.
pattern_rules.quote: When using the `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` events, you can configure a workflow to run only for pull requests that target specific branches.

pattern_rules.rule: To filter on the head branch of a PR the docs say to use a job `if:` with `github.head_ref`, not the `branches` filter.
pattern_rules.quote: To run a job based on the pull request's head branch name (as opposed to the pull request's base branch name), use the `github.head_ref` context in a conditional. For example, this workflow will run whenever a pull request is opened, but the `run_if` job will only execute if the head of the pull request is a branch whose name starts with `releases/`:

pattern_rules.rule: Branch-name glob alphabet is `*`, `**`, `+`, `?`, `!` 'and others'; a literal match of such characters requires escaping each with `\`.
pattern_rules.quote: The `branches`, `branches-ignore`, `tags`, and `tags-ignore` keywords accept glob patterns that use characters like `*`, `**`, `+`, `?`, `!` and others to match more than one branch or tag name. If a name contains any of these characters and you want a literal match, you need to *escape* each of these special characters with `\`.

pattern_rules.rule: Path glob alphabet is described as `*` and `**` wildcards (the cheat sheet additionally shows `?` and `!` in path examples).
pattern_rules.quote: The `paths` and `paths-ignore` keywords accept glob patterns that use the `*` and `**` wildcard characters to match more than one path name.

pattern_rules.rule: Path patterns are anchored: they must match the whole path from the repository root.
pattern_rules.quote: Path patterns must match the whole path, and start from the repository's root.

pattern_rules.rule: Path filters are ignored for tag pushes.
pattern_rules.quote: When using the `push` and `pull_request` events, you can configure a workflow to run based on what file paths are changed. Path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags.

pattern_rules.rule: `paths` is satisfied when at least one changed file matches.
pattern_rules.quote: If at least one path matches a pattern in the `paths` filter, the workflow runs. For example, the following workflow would run anytime you push a JavaScript file (`.js`).

pattern_rules.rule: `paths-ignore` suppresses the run only when ALL changed files match; any single non-matching file makes the workflow run.
pattern_rules.quote: When all the path names match patterns in `paths-ignore`, the workflow will not run. If any path names do not match patterns in `paths-ignore`, even if some path names match the patterns, the workflow will run.

pattern_rules.rule: A literal pattern matches the exact branch/tag name.
pattern_rules.quote: Matches the exact name of a branch or tag name.

pattern_rules.rule: `'**'` is the implicit default when no branches/tags filter is given.
pattern_rules.quote: Matches all branch and tag names. This is the default behavior when you don't use a `branches` or `tags` filter.

pattern_rules.rule: `'**'` is the implicit default when no path filter is given.
pattern_rules.quote: The `**` wildcard matches any character including slash (`/`). This is the default behavior when you don't use a `path` filter.

pattern_rules.rule: `'*'` alone matches only names without a slash.
pattern_rules.quote: Matches all branch and tag names that don't contain a slash (`/`). The `*` character is a special character in YAML. When you start a pattern with `*`, you must use quotes.

pattern_rules.rule: `branches-ignore` / `tags-ignore`: a match means the workflow does not run.
pattern_rules.quote: When a pattern matches the `branches-ignore` or `tags-ignore` pattern, the workflow will not run. The patterns defined in `branches` and `tags` are evaluated against the Git ref's name.

pattern_rules.rule: workflow_run branches filter applies to the branch the TRIGGERING workflow ran on.
pattern_rules.quote: When using the `workflow_run` event, you can specify what branches the triggering workflow must run on in order to trigger your workflow.

pattern_rules.rule: Workflows skipped by branch/path filters leave their checks 'Pending', which blocks merging when those checks are required.
pattern_rules.quote: If a workflow is skipped due to branch filtering, path filtering, or a commit message, then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

pattern_rules.rule: Multiple events are OR-ed; simultaneous events create multiple runs.
pattern_rules.quote: If you specify multiple events, only one of those events needs to occur to trigger your workflow. If multiple triggering events for your workflow occur at the same time, multiple workflow runs will be triggered.

pattern_rules.rule: Multiple activity types are OR-ed; simultaneous activity types create one run each (issue opened with two labels = 3 runs).
pattern_rules.quote: If you specify multiple activity types, only one of those event activity types needs to occur to trigger your workflow. If multiple triggering event activity types for your workflow occur at the same time, multiple workflow runs will be triggered. For example, the following workflow triggers when an issue is opened or labeled. If an issue with two labels is opened, three workflow runs will start: one for the issue opened event and two for the two issue labeled events.

pattern_rules.rule: When mixing configured and unconfigured events, every event must be a mapping key ending in `:`.
pattern_rules.quote: If you specify activity types or filters for an event and your workflow triggers on multiple events, you must configure each event separately. You must append a colon (`:`) to all events, including events without configuration.

pattern_rules.rule: `types` narrows activity; it is unnecessary for single-activity events.
pattern_rules.quote: Use `on.<event_name>.types` to define the type of activity that will trigger a workflow run. Most GitHub events are triggered by more than one type of activity. For example, the `label` is triggered when a label is `created`, `edited`, or `deleted`. The `types` keyword enables you to narrow down activity that causes the workflow to run. When only one activity type triggers a webhook event, the `types` keyword is unnecessary.

pattern_rules.rule: Specifying `types: [created]` on `label` excludes edited/deleted.
pattern_rules.quote: For example, the `issue_comment` event has the `created`, `edited`, and `deleted` activity types. If your workflow triggers on the `label` event, it will run whenever a label is created, edited, or deleted. If you specify the `created` activity type for the `label` event, your workflow will run when a label is created but not when a label is edited or deleted.

pattern_rules.rule: `on: push` with no filter runs for a push to any branch.
pattern_rules.quote:
For example, a workflow with the following `on` value will run when a push is made to any branch in the workflow's repository:

```yaml
on: push
```

pattern_rules.rule: Commit-message skip strings suppress push/pull_request runs (but not pull_request_target).
pattern_rules.quote:
Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

* `[skip ci]`
* `[ci skip]`
* `[no ci]`
* `[skip actions]`
* `[actions skip]`

pattern_rules.rule: Skip instructions apply only to push and pull_request.
pattern_rules.quote: Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

pattern_rules.rule: `skip-checks` commit trailer is an alternative skip mechanism.
pattern_rules.quote:
Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

* `skip-checks:true`
* `skip-checks: true`

pattern_rules.rule: Events caused by GITHUB_TOKEN do not create runs, except workflow_dispatch, repository_dispatch, and pull_request opened/synchronize/reopened (which create approval-required runs).
pattern_rules.quote:
When you use the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` to perform tasks, events triggered by the `GITHUB_TOKEN` will not create a new workflow run, with the following exceptions:

* `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` events always create workflow runs.
* `pull_request` events with the `opened`, `synchronize`, or `reopened` activity types: when a workflow using `GITHUB_TOKEN` creates or updates a pull request, the resulting `pull_request` event creates workflow runs in an **approval-required** state.

pattern_rules.rule: Case sensitivity of glob matching: not documented.
pattern_rules.quote: not documented

pattern_rules.rule: Whether `!` negation is permitted inside `branches-ignore`, `tags-ignore` or `paths-ignore` lists: not documented (docs only show `!` inside `branches`, `tags` and `paths`).
pattern_rules.quote: not documented

pattern_rules.rule: Whether branch/tag patterns are anchored (must match the whole ref name) is not stated explicitly for branches/tags; it is stated only for paths. Examples (e.g. `v2*` matching `v2.9`, `feature/*` matching `feature/my-branch`) are consistent with whole-name matching.
pattern_rules.quote: not documented

Runs your workflow when you push a commit or tag, or when you create a repository from a template. This includes workflows that are not merged into the default branch.

* Events will not be created if more than 5,000 branches are pushed at once. Events will not be created for tags when more than three tags are pushed at once.

GITHUB_REF (variables page): For workflows triggered by `push`, this is the branch or tag ref that was pushed. ... for branches the format is `refs/heads/<branch_name>` ... For tags it is `refs/tags/<tag_name>`.

events.github_ref: PR merge branch `refs/pull/PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER/merge` (closed-and-merged: the fully qualified ref of the branch it was merged into, e.g. `/refs/heads/main`)
events.github_sha: Last merge commit on the `GITHUB_REF` branch
events.quote:
By default, a workflow only runs when a `pull_request` event's activity type is `opened`, `synchronize`, or `reopened`. To trigger workflows by different activity types, use the `types` keyword.

Workflows will not run on `pull_request` activity if the pull request has a merge conflict. The merge conflict must be resolved first.

The value of `GITHUB_REF` varies for a closed pull request depending on whether the pull request has been merged or not. If a pull request was closed but not merged, it will be `refs/pull/PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER/merge`. If a pull request was closed as a result of being merged, it will be the fully qualified `ref` of the branch it was merged into, for example `/refs/heads/main`.

Note that `GITHUB_SHA` for this event is the last merge commit of the pull request merge branch. If you want to get the commit ID for the last commit to the head branch of the pull request, use `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` instead.

* `GITHUB_REF` is set to `refs/pull/PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER/merge`
* `GITHUB_SHA` is the SHA of the merge commit on the merge branch

This event runs in the context of the default branch of the base repository, rather than in the context of the merge commit, as the `pull_request` event does.

path_filter_rules.rule: Path filters compare the changed-file list against `paths`/`paths-ignore`; zero changed files means no run.
path_filter_rules.quote: The filter determines if a workflow should run by evaluating the changed files and running them against the `paths-ignore` or `paths` list. If there are no files changed, the workflow will not run.

path_filter_rules.rule: Changed files: two-dot diff for pushes, three-dot diff for pull requests.
path_filter_rules.quote: GitHub generates the list of changed files using two-dot diffs for pushes and three-dot diffs for pull requests:

path_filter_rules.rule: pull_request: three-dot diff = topic branch tip vs merge base with the base branch.
path_filter_rules.quote: **Pull requests:** Three-dot diffs are a comparison between the most recent version of the topic branch and the commit where the topic branch was last synced with the base branch.

path_filter_rules.rule: push to existing branch: two-dot diff of before/after SHAs.
path_filter_rules.quote: **Pushes to existing branches:** A two-dot diff compares the head and base SHAs directly with each other.

path_filter_rules.rule: push to a new branch: two-dot diff against the parent of the deepest pushed commit's ancestor.
path_filter_rules.quote: **Pushes to new branches:** A two-dot diff against the parent of the ancestor of the deepest commit pushed.

path_filter_rules.rule: Limit: a push with more than 1,000 commits ALWAYS runs regardless of path filter.
path_filter_rules.quote: If a push contains more than 1,000 commits, the workflow will **always** run.

path_filter_rules.rule: Limit: diff generation timeout means the workflow ALWAYS runs.
path_filter_rules.quote: If generating the diff times out, the workflow will **always** run.

path_filter_rules.rule: Limit: diff with more than 3,000 files where the matching files are not in the first 3,000 means the workflow does NOT run.
path_filter_rules.quote: If the generated diff contains more than 3,000 files and the files the workflow filter matches are not in the first 3,000 returned by the filter, the workflow will **not** run.

path_filter_rules.rule: Remedy suggested by docs when limits bite.
path_filter_rules.quote: If you observe these behaviors, you might need to make your filters more specific, or change how you work with pushes and pull requests to generate simpler diffs.

path_filter_rules.rule: Path filters are not evaluated for tag pushes (tag pushes are governed by tags/tags-ignore only).
path_filter_rules.quote: Path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags.

path_filter_rules.rule: `paths`: at least one changed file must match.
path_filter_rules.quote: If at least one path matches a pattern in the `paths` filter, the workflow runs.

path_filter_rules.rule: `paths-ignore`: run is suppressed only when every changed file matches.
path_filter_rules.quote: When all the path names match patterns in `paths-ignore`, the workflow will not run. If any path names do not match patterns in `paths-ignore`, even if some path names match the patterns, the workflow will run.

path_filter_rules.rule: `paths`/`paths-ignore` AND `branches`/`branches-ignore`: both must be satisfied (push).
path_filter_rules.quote: If you define both `branches`/`branches-ignore` and `paths`/`paths-ignore`, the workflow will only run when both filters are satisfied.

path_filter_rules.rule: `paths`/`paths-ignore` AND `branches`/`branches-ignore`: both must be satisfied (pull_request / pull_request_target).
path_filter_rules.quote: If you use both the `branches` filter and the `paths` filter, the workflow will only run when both filters are satisfied. For example, the following workflow will only run when a pull request that includes a change to a JavaScript (`.js`) file is opened on a branch whose name starts with `releases/`:

path_filter_rules.rule: Mixing `paths` and `paths-ignore` on one event is not allowed; use `!` inside `paths`.
path_filter_rules.quote: You cannot use both the `paths` and `paths-ignore` filters for the same event in a workflow. If you want to both include and exclude path patterns for a single event, use the `paths` filter prefixed with the `!` character to indicate which paths should be excluded.

path_filter_rules.rule: Sequential negation semantics for paths.
path_filter_rules.quote:
The order that you define `paths` patterns matters:

* A matching negative pattern (prefixed with `!`) after a positive match will exclude the path.
* A matching positive pattern after a negative match will include the path again.

path_filter_rules.rule: Path filters are available on push, pull_request and pull_request_target (section title lists exactly these events).
path_filter_rules.quote:
## `on.<push|pull_request|pull_request_target>.<paths|paths-ignore>`

When using the `push` and `pull_request` events, you can configure a workflow to run based on what file paths are changed.

path_filter_rules.rule: The push payload seen by Actions does not contain per-commit added/removed/modified file lists, so a simulator cannot derive changed files from `github.event.commits[*]`.
path_filter_rules.quote: The webhook payload available to GitHub Actions does not include the `added`, `removed`, and `modified` attributes in the `commit` object. You can retrieve the full commit object using the API.

path_filter_rules.rule: Definition of three-dot vs two-dot diff (Branches reference page the filter docs link to).
path_filter_rules.quote:
| Three-dot | `git diff A...B` | The most recent common commit of both branches (merge base) and the most recent version of the topic branch.    |
| Two-dot   | `git diff A..B`  | The most recent state of the base branch (for example, `main`) and the most recent version of the topic branch. |

path_filter_rules.rule: Three-dot focuses on what the PR introduces; two-dot changes when base moves.
path_filter_rules.quote:
Because the three-dot comparison uses the merge base, it focuses on "what a pull request introduces."

When you use a two-dot comparison, the diff changes when the base branch is updated, even if you haven't made any changes to the topic branch.

path_filter_rules.rule: Skipped-by-path-filter workflows leave checks Pending and block merges that require them.
path_filter_rules.quote: If a workflow is skipped due to path filtering, branch filtering, or a commit message, then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

For workflows triggered by `push`, this is the branch or tag ref that was pushed. For workflows triggered by `pull_request` that were not merged, this is the pull request merge branch. If the pull request was merged, this is the branch it was merged into. For workflows triggered by `release`, this is the release tag created. For other triggers, this is the branch or tag ref that triggered the workflow run. This is only set if a branch or tag is available for the event type. The ref given is fully-formed, meaning that for branches the format is `refs/heads/<branch_name>`. For pull request events except `pull_request_target` that were not merged, it is `refs/pull/<pr_number>/merge`. `pull_request_target` events have the `ref` from the base branch. For tags it is `refs/tags/<tag_name>`. For example, `refs/heads/feature-branch-1`." — https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables and https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context.
